note: agent-guard runs this CLI to distribute an already-scanned skill into every agent on the machine, and in project mode to stage a pinned commit (owner/repo#sha) into a throw-away directory before the scan. GuardDog returns BLOCK on the same four findings as for 1.5.26; each is accepted with a reason AND neutralised by how the wrapper invokes the CLI (npm_config_ignore_scripts=true, reduced environment without credentials). New in 1.7.0 compared with 1.5.26: Notion as a skill source (notion / notion.so URLs, needs the separate `ntn` CLI); agent-guard only passes GitHub owner/repo#sha or local paths, so that code path is never reached. Any other finding, in this or a later version, stops delegation and the built-in installer takes over.

findings.reason: husky is the package's own git-hook tooling for development. npm runs `prepare` only on publish/pack, on an argument-less local `npm install`, on `npm install <folder>` and for git dependencies -- never for a registry tarball and not under npx. The wrapper additionally sets npm_config_ignore_scripts=true, so no lifecycle script can run at all.

Documented feature: the CLI reads a GitHub token and sends it only as the Authorization header of its GitHub requests, to reach private repositories. agent-guard stages public repositories, and the delegated process runs with a reduced environment that contains no token variables.
Same private-repository code path as GITHUB_TOKEN, reading the GitHub CLI's variable. Not present in the reduced environment the wrapper passes.
Agent detection: the presence of COPILOT_* variables identifies a GitHub Copilot session. The value is used as a signal, and the variable is not present in the reduced environment the wrapper passes.
